title: I’m building a Habbo/Sims-inspired multiplayer world with AI assistance, and the hardest part so far has been the art direction
author: nobodyeverimportant
selftext:
I’ve been working on an independent browser-based multiplayer social game inspired by Habbo Hotel, The Sims 1/2, and the weird, wonderful early-2000s internet.

The goal is eventually to create a virtual world where people can socialize, customize avatars, attend events, and help shape the community.

I’ve been using ChatGPT for development planning and prototyping, with Claude and Gemini providing additional design exploration and technical reviews.

One of the biggest things I’ve learned so far is that AI can help you explore ideas incredibly quickly, but getting a consistent, genuinely distinctive visual identity is another story entirely. 😭

Some of my early experiments were technically interesting but looked far too generic or geometric. I’ve actually hiring with my artist friend for character concepts while continuing to use AI for technical assistance.

I’m still in the early stages, with a small closed beta planned for February 2027.  
I’m curious how other developers are handling this:  
**Have you found AI more useful for programming and prototyping than for establishing a cohesive art direction?**

And for anyone combining AI tools with human artists, how are you organizing that workflow?  
I’d love to hear what’s worked for you, especially if you’re building something larger than a single-player game.
